candidates.attacker_control: The sizes/counts come from the archive itself: the 20-byte start header (nextHeaderOffset/nextHeaderSize/nextHeaderCrc, read at lines 292-302) and the next-header structures parsed by readStreamsInfo/readPackInfo/readUnpackInfo/readFilesInfo. An attacker who can get a victim to open an untrusted .7z (SevenZFile(File/SeekableByteChannel) constructors) fully controls these values; the CRC32VerifyingInputStream checks are satisfiable because the attacker computes the CRC over the crafted header.
candidates.counterevidence_checked: Checked that the start-header CRC and next-header CRC are verified (CRC32VerifyingInputStream, lines 270-274): attacker can compute correct CRCs, so this is not a barrier. Checked that nextHeaderSizeInt != nextHeaderSize rejects values > Integer.MAX_VALUE (lines 263-266): values up to 2^31-1 still reach allocate(). Checked that IOUtils.readFully on a short file throws EOFException: the allocation precedes the read, so OOM still occurs. Checked for any size sanity checks or memory-limit plumbing for 7z in this snapshot: none found (memory limits exist only for LZMA/XZ/Z streams).
candidates.impact: Denial of service: heap exhaustion (OutOfMemoryError) or NegativeArraySizeException while opening/parsing a crafted archive, taking down or degrading any service that processes untrusted 7z files; repeated requests can sustain the DoS. Potential memory-pressure side effects are bounded by the JVM heap.
candidates.prerequisites: Victim parses an attacker-supplied 7z archive with SevenZFile; no memoryLimit is enforced (the API in this version exposes no limit for 7z); only a finite heap is needed for the OOM to become a DoS. The start-header cast check (lines 263-266) only rejects values that do not fit in a signed int, not excessively large ints.
candidates.root_cause: SevenZFile reads 64-bit length/count fields out of the (CRC-checked, attacker-produced) 7z start header and header structures and feeds them directly into allocations after only truncating casts. There is no upper bound and no configurable memory limit in this version: readHeaders() casts startHeader.nextHeaderSize to int and calls ByteBuffer.allocate(nextHeaderSizeInt) (line 268) before reading any of that data from the channel; readArchiveProperties allocates new byte[(int) propertySize] (line 338); readPackInfo allocates new long[(int) numPackStreams] for packSizes/packCrcs (lines 406, 415); readUnpackInfo allocates new Folder[(int) numFolders] (line 436) and long[totalOutputStreams] (line 451); coders allocate new byte[(int) propertiesSize] (line 588); readFilesInfo allocates new byte[(int)(size - 1)] (line 710); readEncodedHeader allocates new byte[(int) folder.getUnpackSize()] (line 368). Values whose int truncation is negative also produce NegativeArraySizeException, and values such as 0x7FFFFFFF produce multi-gigabyte requests that the JVM cannot satisfy.
candidates.title: SevenZFile allocates attacker-controlled sizes from 7z header fields without bounds (OOM DoS)
candidates.trace: SevenZFile.readHeaders() -> readStartHeader() reads nextHeaderSize as an unchecked little-endian long (lines 298-300) -> (int) cast accepted if <= Integer.MAX_VALUE -> channel.position(SIGNATURE_HEADER_SIZE + nextHeaderOffset) -> ByteBuffer.allocate(nextHeaderSizeInt) at line 268 allocates solely on the declared size (IOUtils.readFully later throws EOFException for a short file, but the allocation has already happened) -> OOM. Independently, readArchiveProperties (line 338), readPackInfo (lines 406/415), readUnpackInfo (lines 436/451), Coder properties (line 588) and readFilesInfo (line 710) allocate arrays from header-declared counts/lengths before validating them against the remaining header size, and readEncodedHeader (line 368) allocates the decoded-header buffer from folder.getUnpackSize().
candidates.unverified: Not runtime-confirmed: no archive was built or executed. Exact allocation thresholds and which of the multiple sites triggers first depend on JVM heap and archive shape. Whether a given embedder catches OutOfMemoryError/NegativeArraySizeException is deployment-specific. The relation index has no data/control-flow and only parsed a subset of Java files, so no guarantee that every path into these allocations was enumerated.
candidates.weakness_type: CWE-789 (Memory Allocation with Excessive Size Value) / CWE-400 (Uncontrolled Resource Consumption)

summary: Reviewed Apache Commons Compress at version 1.16-SNAPSHOT (changes.xml latest entry COMPRESS-430, dated 2017-11-25). The strongest source-evidenced issue is in the 7z reader: SevenZFile allocates buffers/arrays directly from attacker-controlled header fields with no size validation and no memory-limit option, so a small crafted .7z archive can exhaust the JVM heap (CWE-789/CWE-400; same class as the later official Commons Compress 7z memory-exhaustion advisory). Static review only; no runtime confirmation. I could not identify a confidently date-matched 1.16-era reference fix, so this is submitted as the single best-supported candidate.
